title: Console walkthrough — usage analytics & cost breakdown (Sable Retail)
summary: AE+SE walkthrough of Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating migration from mixed self-hosted endpoints + OpenAI, concerned about per-route cost, PKI/KMS integration, and ability to run canaries and spend guardrails. Agreed next steps: send pricing + pilot plan, share SOC2/KMS docs, schedule a 1-week benchmark/pilot starting next Monday.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya will take us through the console and cost deep dive. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lena: Doing good, thanks. We have about 45 minutes, want to cover analytics and the cost bits, and then security quick Q's.
[00:13] Priya: Great, I'll share my screen — can you confirm you can see the Redwood Console? (small pause) Looks like it's coming up.
[00:28] Raj: Yep, screen's visible. Sorry, connection was a bit slow.
[00:31] Priya: No worries. So first slide is just context: typical routes, token profiles, and how we attribute cost to routes. We'll jump into live console — first thing, usage analytics at the org and route level.
[00:45] Jordan: Quick note — our standard telemetry is token-level, we break down generated vs. prompt tokens, and we show per-route latency percentiles and cost.
[00:55] Priya: Alright switching to Console > Analytics. You'll see the top of the page gives a time window, global token volume, and cost estimate. For Sable this demo tenant has three routes: search-assist, checkout-chat, and feedback-embedding.
[01:12] Priya: You can filter by model family — here we see routes pinned to redwood/gpt-2-7b (note: not an actual customer model) and open variants. The Cost Breakdown panel is where the magic is — it decomposes spend by model, by route, and by compute footprint (dedicated vs hosted).
[01:30] Raj: Quick question — we run a mix of on-prem and cloud; will the console show both?
[01:36] Priya: Yes, as long as the private deployment reports metrics to the control plane. For on-prem we collect usage via the agent and attribute to the account; you get per-region and per-deployment visibility. There can be a short lag depending on retention and ingestion.
[01:50] [02:02] Mark: How accurate is the cost estimate? We ran into estimates being off in other tools.
[02:07] Priya: Good question. The estimate is modelled from your configured instance cost (GPU type pricing), quantization profile, and token accounting. For hosted accounts we use Redwood's published unit costs and your discounts. For Dedicated/Private, you input the infra hourly cost and we amortize it across tokens; it's an estimate but matches within about 5–10% for steady-state workloads. There can be variance during bursts.
[02:33] Lena: Can you show a per-route cost example?
[02:36] Priya: Sure. Switching to route view. Here — you'll see a stacked bar chart: prompt vs gen tokens, then a cost line overlay. For checkout-chat you can see higher latency p95 but lower token count; search-assist has high token volume and that's our biggest cost driver.
[02:52] Priya: Notice the attribution toggle — you can choose to attribute KV cache hits to the request or exclude them. Some customers prefer excluding cache hits when calculating per-request SLA cost.
[03:07] Raj: Hmm that matters for us, because we heavily rely on prefix caching.
[03:10] Priya: Exactly. There's also an effective tokens per request metric that accounts for cache reuse.
[03:20] [03:34] Jordan: The Route Details page also surfaces model variant rollouts — you can see traffic split, quality metrics, and cost delta between variants. Priya, maybe show the canary UI?
[03:42] Priya: Yep. Canary rollouts are under Deployments > Rollouts. You can pick a route, select baseline model and candidate, define percent ramp, and set automatic rollback if latency or cost thresholds spike.
[03:55] Mark: Automatic rollback on cost? That's interesting — we want to avoid runaway spend during bad rollouts.
[04:01] Priya: You set a cost-per-token budget per minute or per hour and an SLA for latency. If candidate causes cost to go above threshold, it can automatically shift traffic back.
[04:12] [04:25] Lena: For security, Tara wants to know how audit logs appear for these changes.
[04:29] Tara: Yes, we need immutable logs for deployments and key access.
[04:33] Priya: Audit logs are exported to your configured SIEM (we support syslog/S3/Kafka) and include user, action, timestamp, and request identifiers. For Private, logs can be kept in your VPC and we support HSM/KMS for key material.
[04:49] Tara: Do you integrate with our Okta SAML and with our cloud KMS?
[04:54] Priya: Yes to both — SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported, RBAC roles map to console permissions, and we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HashiCorp Vault for model key encryption.
[05:06] Samir: Any latency overhead for KMS? If every request needs envelope decryption we worry about token path latency.
[05:13] Priya: We use envelope encryption and cache decrypted keys in-memory on the inference nodes; KMS calls happen during model load or rotation, not per token, so minimal impact on per-token latency.
[05:26] [05:38] Priya: Back to analytics: here's the per-route histogram and trend. See the 'cost per 1k requests' metric — you can click any bar to drill into the raw requests and sample prompts (redacted automatically).
[05:50] Raj: Are prompts redacted by default? We have PII concerns.
[05:55] Priya: Yes, PII redaction is configurable. By default we mask emails/ssns and you can opt out of storing raw prompts entirely — we'll still keep aggregates and embeddings if needed.
[06:06] Jordan: Also call out that for HIPAA settings we have stricter retention and you can opt for on-prem only ingestion.
[06:13] Lena: Good. Show us the cost breakdown exported to CSV — ops wants a weekly billback.
[06:18] Priya: Export is under Reports. You can generate a cost allocation report that splits spend by team, route, and tag. We support tagging routes with project/team metadata so FinOps can billback.
[06:31] [06:48] Priya: Now a quick demo of the cost comparison wizard — you can simulate switching quantization profiles or moving from hosted to dedicated. Input expected QPS and average length, and the wizard shows expected monthly cost and latency tradeoffs.
[06:59] Raj: Could you run one for our search-assist? QPS 120, avg 120 tokens, candidate quant to int8.
[07:07] Priya: Running the sim... shows ~22% cost reduction with 8-bit quantization, ~10–15ms added tail latency depending on hardware. There's also a note about potential regen-quality delta — we tie that to your eval sets.
[07:22] Raj: We'll need to run evals.
[07:24] Priya: Totally. The Console links to Redwood Optimize where you can run batch evals against a ground-truth set and surface quality regressions per rollout.
[07:34] [07:50] Mark: On the billing side, how granular is the data? We need per-route, per-customer, per-day.
[07:56] Priya: We have hourly granularity and per-request identifiers for traceability. You can also stream event-level logs to your billing pipeline.
[08:07] Lena: Do you expose an API for pulling these metrics programmatically?
[08:11] Priya: Yes, Analytics API v1 — endpoints to pull aggregated metrics and raw request samples (if retention enabled). We'll send a token scoped only for metrics.
[08:19] [08:32] Jordan: Quick interruption — competitors were mentioned earlier; how do we position vs Anthropic or huge cloud PaaS?
[08:39] Lena: We're evaluating Anthropic for model quality, and we're on OpenAI for some routes. Latency and cost are the deciding factors.
[08:48] Jordan: Redwood's pitch is production control — predictable cost, rollouts, private deployment options.
[08:54] Priya: Back to the console: I'll show a live cost drill for last 30 days. You can change the time window and apply tags; here's a spike on Aug 18 where an unbounded scrape caused 20% spike. We surfaced an alert and auto-throttled by policy.
[09:10] Raj: Nice. We need that — last time a script ramped us and we had surprise spend.
[09:15] Priya: Alerts are configurable per-route and can send to PagerDuty/Slack/email.
[09:21] [09:33] Priya: Now on to per-route dashboard layout: top-left KPIs (reqs, tokens, cost, avg latency p50/p95), mid shows traffic split, bottom has raw samples and error traces. You can pin widgets and save custom dashboards.
[09:48] Mark: Can we make dashboards read-only for execs?
[09:51] Priya: Yes RBAC supports viewer vs editor vs admin. We can map Okta groups to those roles.
[09:58] Tara: For compliance, is the audit log tamper-evident?
[10:03] Priya: We provide signed log bundles and support WORM S3 buckets for retention.
[10:10] [10:21] Priya: I want to show an example cost report for a mixed deployment — here it splits hosted usage (applies hosted unit rates) and dedicated infra cost which we amortize. You can choose allocation strategy: by tokens, by requests, or fixed percent.
[10:36] Raj: For Dedicated, how do you handle GPU pooling and contention? We'd like per-route guarantees.
[10:42] Priya: Dedicated capacity supports configurable queue priorities and pool pinning. You can pin a route to a pool with guaranteed reserved slots and burst to shared pool when idle.
[10:54] [11:05] Jordan: We also support soft SLOs per route that trade cost vs latency; the console surfaces expected cost impact of SLO changes.
[11:13] Priya: Quick demo: lowering p95 latency SLO from 200ms to 120ms shows cost increase and suggested quant/hardware.
[11:25] Mark: Ok that's useful.
[11:28] [11:40] Priya: Now let's simulate a canary where candidate model is cheaper but slightly higher latency — here's the traffic split and expected delta. You can set auto-fallback to baseline after X minutes if quality or cost deviates.
[11:53] Raj: Do you capture hallucination/regression signals automatically?
[11:58] Priya: We capture downstream metrics (e.g., click-through or conversion if you send events) and tie them to route performance. For hallucination detection we rely on your eval sets and RW Optimize's automatic scoring; there's also an optional human-in-the-loop review queue.
[12:14] [12:30] Lena: Ok, a few practical items — 1) we need to know how to tag routes by product line, 2) we need daily cost exports to our finance bucket, and 3) security needs the SOC2 docs and key rotation details.
[12:43] Jordan: Great — we'll follow up with a package.
[12:46] Priya: I'll pause the live demo and switch to a short Q&A.
[12:53] Tara: On data residency: can we keep analytics data in our EU region only?
[12:58] Priya: Yes for Private we support region-limited control plane and data residency. Hosted has region options but check specifics for log retention. We'll send region compliance matrix.
[13:12] Samir: For our pilot, can we run a 1-week benchmark using a snapshot of traffic? We want to compare latency/cost vs our current stack.
[13:20] Priya: Absolutely — we typically run a one-week pilot: we ingest traffic through a traffic-shaping proxy or replay, and run side-by-side comparisons. We'll provide a runbook and suggested dataset size.
[13:33] Raj: We need per-route SLA definitions too for the pilot.
[13:37] Jordan: We'll propose SLAs in the pilot doc.
[13:41] [13:50] Lena: Any red flags we've missed?
[13:53] Mark: Only around integration effort — how long to get telemetry and tagging in place?
[13:59] Priya: For a basic setup with two routes and tagging, we estimate 2–3 days of engineering plus a short onboarding call. Private/on-prem can take longer depending on firewall and KMS.
[14:11] Raj: What about cost of Dedicated — do you have an example?
[14:16] Priya: We'll include a sample Dedicated sizing and pricing table in the follow-up. For example, a 4-GPU pool for 150 QPS of 512 tokens could land in X range — we'll send concrete numbers based on your QPS and token profile.
[14:32] [14:45] Jordan: Ok, recap next steps: Jordan to send pricing + pilot plan, Priya to share SOC2/KMS integration docs and runbook for benchmark, and schedule pilot kickoff for next Monday if that works for Sable.
[14:58] Lena: Next Monday works. Can we have an initial SOW draft before Friday?
[15:02] Jordan: Yes we'll aim for Friday EOD.
[15:07] Tara: Also please include the retention policy options for PII redaction.
[15:11] Priya: We'll include that.
[15:15] [15:20] (small cross talk while attendees check calendars)
[15:43] Jordan: Any final questions?
[15:48] Samir: No, thanks — excited to run the pilot.
[15:51] Raj: Thanks everyone.
[15:53] Lena: Thanks.
next_steps: Jordan to send pricing and pilot SOW by Friday EOD
Priya to share SOC2, KMS integration doc, and pilot runbook (incl. replay/run instructions)
Schedule pilot kickoff next Monday; capture required telemetry and tags beforehand
